passage: I'm Asif, and I live across from Vasudha's family. She's about two. Whenever the pressure cooker whistles, she drops everything and covers her ears, face scrunched. At her cousin's birthday she clung to her mother's leg for a long time before joining the others. Her cousin, the same age, runs straight into any crowd. I don't know what Vasudha feels inside, but loud sounds and new places seem to hit her harder.

qa.q: What does Vasudha do when the pressure cooker whistles?
qa.a: She drops everything and covers her ears, face scrunched.

qa.q: What might Vasudha's clinging at the birthday suggest?
qa.a: It might suggest she needs more time to feel comfortable in new, busy places.

qa.q: How could Vasudha's parents support her?
qa.a: They could give her time to warm up and warn her before loud sounds.

qa.q: How does Asif see the difference between Vasudha and her cousin?
qa.a: Asif notices her cousin runs straight in while loud sounds and new places seem to affect Vasudha more.

grounding: A neighbour observes a toddler's sensory sensitivity and slower adaptability compared with a cousin.

passage:
Monday: Yusuf screamed when Shreya put on his new wool sweater, tugging at the neck.
Thursday: At the mall, he burst into tears at the music. Shreya carried him outside, where he calmed.
Two weeks later: Shreya chose soft cotton shirts and planned a quieter family visit. Yusuf played happily, only covering his ears once when the doorbell rang.

qa.q: What did Yusuf tug at on Monday?
qa.a: He tugged at the neck of his new wool sweater.

qa.q: Why did Yusuf burst into tears at the mall?
qa.a: The loud music seemed too much for his senses and upset him.

qa.q: What changes did Shreya make to help Yusuf?
qa.a: Shreya chose soft cotton shirts and planned quieter visits to suit his sensitivity.

qa.q: How might Shreya's view of Yusuf have changed over these weeks?
qa.a: Shreya may now see his reactions as his sensitive nature rather than naughtiness.

grounding: It shows a toddler's sensory sensitivity and a caregiver adjusting to his temperament over time.

passage: At the colony park in Hyderabad, the new sprinkler burst on. Bhavna, two, shrieked with joy and ran straight in, soaking her frock. Her twin, Alka, stopped at the edge. She held out one finger, touched a drop, then pulled back and watched. Mummy sat beside her. After a long while, Alka stepped in, just one foot.

qa.q: What did Bhavna do when the sprinkler burst on?
qa.a: She shrieked with joy and ran straight in, soaking her frock.

qa.q: What does Alka touching a drop and pulling back suggest?
qa.a: It suggests she is cautious and needs time to test new things before joining in.

qa.q: How did Mummy support Alka?
qa.a: She sat beside her and let her take her time rather than pushing her in.

qa.q: Why might Bhavna and Alka react so differently?
qa.a: Each twin has her own temperament: Bhavna is bold, while Alka is slower to warm up.

grounding: It shows two toddlers with different baseline reactivity and adaptability.

passage:
"Arohi, it's just the pressure cooker," Jasleen said, but Arohi was already under the table, hands over her ears.

"Too loud! Too loud!"

"Okay, okay." Jasleen crouched. "Want to come to the balcony till it's done?"

Arohi nodded and climbed into her arms.

On the balcony, Arohi's Papa called from inside, "She's so sensitive. Her cousin sleeps through fireworks."

"She's just made differently," Jasleen said. "Next time I'll take her out before the whistle."

qa.q: What sound made Arohi hide under the table?
qa.a: The pressure cooker whistle made her hide.

qa.q: What was Arohi feeling under the table?
qa.a: She felt overwhelmed and frightened by the loud sound, covering her ears and saying it was too loud.

qa.q: What plan did Jasleen make, and why is it helpful?
qa.a: She decided to take Arohi outside before the whistle next time, which works with Arohi's sensitivity instead of forcing her to endure it.

qa.q: How does Arohi's Papa seem to see her reaction?
qa.a: He compares her to her cousin and seems a bit puzzled or worried that she reacts so strongly.

grounding: A home dialogue shows a toddler's strong sensitivity to noise and an adult adapting to her temperament.

passage:
Note from Vaibhav, playgroup teacher, Monday:

Suraj, two and a half, is our slow-to-warm-up friend. He stands at the door for about ten minutes each morning, watching, before he joins. At music time today he covered his ears when the drum started, but he tapped softly on the table with one finger. Scratchy labels bother him too.

What I did next: I let him watch first, gave him a small soft shaker instead of the drum, and asked his parents about his clothes.

qa.q: What did Suraj do when the drum started?
qa.a: He covered his ears but tapped softly on the table with one finger.

qa.q: What does Suraj's soft tapping suggest?
qa.a: It suggests he wanted to join the music but felt overwhelmed by the drum's loudness, so he joined in a quieter way.

qa.q: How did Vaibhav adjust things for Suraj's temperament?
qa.a: Vaibhav let Suraj watch before joining and gave him a softer shaker, respecting his pace and sensitivity.

qa.q: How might Suraj's parents see this note?
qa.a: They may feel reassured that the teacher understands their son and is working with his needs.

grounding: A teacher's note describes a toddler's cautious, sound- and touch-sensitive temperament and how the teacher adjusted.
